category_feedback.specific_evidence: Blueprint A8.1 text reads 'demonstrate an understanding of categorizing objects and information' but input_row.json A8.1 reads 'sort objects or data using one attribute' — the lesson references the blueprint version and never bridges forward to Lesson 2's counting arc; expanded_walkthrough does not cross-reference Day 2.
category_feedback.required_fix: Update curriculum_expectations text to byte-match input_row.json ('sort objects or data using one attribute'), and add an explicit forward bridge in the consolidation teacher_script — e.g., 'Tomorrow Tally the Tally Cat will help us COUNT each group we sorted today; remember your sort attribute, you'll need it.'

category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough.title names a real K trap (multi-attribute confusion: child puts a red big button in BOTH 'red' and 'big' piles) but cites no research and recovery_moves do not branch by what the diagnostic tells you about the child — recovery is a single linear sequence (today's-attribute card, drill, show same-set different-sorts).
category_feedback.required_fix: Cite research grounding (Inhelder & Piaget 1964 class-inclusion, or Sarama & Clements 2009 sorting trajectories) in expanded_walkthrough.rationale. Split recovery_moves into a branched diagnostic: if child can name an attribute but misapplies it, use the today's-attribute card; if child cannot name any attribute, drop back to same/different matching with two objects before re-introducing sorting.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: duration_minutes is 50 (12 minds_on + 25 action + 13 consolidation) but the rubric specifies K lessons should be 30–40 minutes — 50 min is a Grade 2/3 budget and will not fit a Kindergarten block; the no-materials body-sort is buried inside differentiation.for_movement_learners rather than offered as an explicit primary alternative.
category_feedback.required_fix: Trim total to 35–40 min: cut action from three 7-min rotations to two 8-min, shorten consolidation to 8 min. Promote the body-sort into an explicit no-paper alternative in lesson_specific_materials: 'No-materials version: sort the CHILDREN themselves by eye colour, shoe type, or shirt colour — bodies become the buttons.'

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Detective Dot anchors minds_on and consolidation and success_criteria all start with 'I can', but there is no quotable refrain or memorable chant the children carry between lessons — exit_routine is 'I sorted by ___' which is a sentence frame, not a Detective Dot signature line.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add a Detective Dot signature refrain children chant back at the close of every lesson, e.g., 'ONE attribute — ONE sort — ONE detective on the case!' Insert it into the consolidation.exit_routine and the teacher_script so children rehearse it; threaded_vocabulary or pedagogical_notes should flag this as the recurring chant for Lessons 2-5.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Conceptual progression is explicit (one attribute at a time, same-set/different-sorts) but expanded_walkthrough.rationale describes the misconception only as 'multi-attribute confusion' without naming the research-grounded construct (class-inclusion); children execute teacher-picked attributes rather than inventing or comparing strategies.
category_feedback.required_fix: In expanded_walkthrough.rationale, name the construct (Piaget & Inhelder 1964 class-inclusion: child cannot yet hold a superordinate and subcategory simultaneously, which is why a red-big button looks like it belongs in two piles). Add a strategy-compare step in action.steps where two pairs share Station C sorts and the class votes which gives 'more groups' or 'easier-to-count groups'.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Worksheet Parts 1, 2, 3 (sort by colour, sort by size, pick own attribute) are a near-exact rote repeat of Stations A, B, C in the lesson action — there is no transfer task or deliberate variation to verify generalization, and image_assets do not include the M9 data anchor chart or M10 Detective Dot poster manipulatives used in the lesson.
category_feedback.required_fix: Convert Part 3 from 'pick your own attribute' (mirrors Station C) into a transfer task: show a pre-sorted set with one item placed in the WRONG group; ask the child to circle the misplaced item and write the attribute being used. This verifies they can read someone else's sort. Add a justification in worksheet_brief noting Part 3 is a transfer task with 1–2 trick items.

summary: Pair 1 is solid Achieving across the board but does not clear the Exceeding bar in any category — six 3s, zero 4s. Lesson is over-budget for K (50 min vs 30–40), trap lacks research citation and branched recovery, character has no quotable refrain, and the worksheet rote-repeats lesson stations instead of transferring. Fixes are concrete and span both lesson and worksheet, hence revise_both.
